correct_diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis (lower urinary tract infection) in a young woman
matching_criterion: Acute uncomplicated cystitis / uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection in a non-pregnant woman. Any wording that names uncomplicated cystitis or lower UTI counts as correct; pyelonephritis or complicated UTI does not.

management_reference.management: Treat with a first-line oral antibiotic for uncomplicated cystitis: fosfomycin trometamol, nitrofurantoin or pivmecillinam (local resistance permitting).
management_reference.source_quote: fosfomycin trometamol, nitrofurantoin, pivmecillinam, alternatively oral cephalosporins

management_reference.management: A urine culture is not required in a young woman with a first uncomplicated episode when the diagnosis is clear from history.
management_reference.source_quote: urine culture is not recommended when a robust diagnosis can be reached by patient history-taking and other potential causes of symptoms can be excluded

management_reference.management: Trimethoprim or co-trimoxazole only if the local E. coli resistance is below 20%.
management_reference.source_quote: Trimethoprim or cotrimoxazole are only recommended if the local resistance pattern for E. coli is <20%

management_scoring_note: Only items with a verified source quote are scored; general good practice that the article does not state is not scored.
